description: Contribute content, Slack-visible: text posts a message (to a channel, DM, or thread — a thread reply can also go to the channel); text+at schedules it for Slack to send later, and cancel withdraws a scheduled one; files attaches up to 10 files from the exchange directory to one message, with text as its comment; emoji+messageTs adds or removes a reaction — a reaction is a small say. This is a write; everything it posts is attributed to your user. You are writing from this account's owner's account. Speak as yourself, the assistant, for this account's owner, in a way that suits the conversation. Don't commit this account's owner to substance they haven't given you. Everything say sends is scanned for secrets before anything is sent; a block can quarantine its destination. Never rework content (encode, split, rename, rephrase) to get it past the scanner.

at.description: With text: schedule the message for Slack to send at this time instead of now, 2 minutes to 120 days out. RFC 3339 with an offset ('2026-10-02T09:00:00-06:00'), a date and time with no offset (read in your Slack profile zone; refused if this machine's zone disagrees), or Unix seconds. Not with files or emoji.

broadcast.description: With thread: also post the reply to the channel (Slack's 'Also send to #channel'). An error without thread, or with emoji.

cancel.description: Withdraw a scheduled message: its handle from say at= or messages scheduled=true. On its own; to is not needed.

emoji.description: Reaction mode: emoji name without colons ('thumbsup'); requires messageTs

files.description: Attach files, at most 10, as one message: bare names inside the exchange directory (the directory download saves into), not paths. Copy a file in first, or write it with put when your file tools cannot reach that directory. Not with emoji or broadcast.

messageTs.description: Reaction mode: the message to react to

remove.description: Reaction mode: remove instead of add

text.description: The message to post; with files, the comment the files are shared with

to.description: Where: '#channel', '@handle' (a DM needs the exact handle, or '@me'), or a channel ID

name: say
